question.text: If <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math> is the origin and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math>, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></math> are distinct tangents to the circle <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the circumcentre of the triangle <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Tangents drawn from the point O, meet the cirle at P & Q and C be the centre of given circle. Then points O, P, C and Q are concyclic. That means any circle passing through O, P and Q also passes through C and OC is the diameter for this circle. Hence mid point of OC is the circumcentre of triangle OPQ.




Coordinates of circumcenter =-g2,-f2
